title: Beyond Fashion Vocabulary: Spatial Style Navigation Through Dual-Layer Style-Structural Mapping in XR.
abstract: We argue that forcing users to describe visual aesthetics with text represents a fundamental architectural flaw in digital fashion systems. We propose a dual-layer framework as a conceptual alternative that reframes style discovery from a linguistic task to a spatial navigation experience in eXtended Reality (XR). The system's upper layer maps fashion styles into a navigable 3D manifold based on 15 affective dimensions derived from Kansei Engineering. The lower layer contains 3,000 designer-curated outfit configurations with detailed structural annotations. Users explore the style landscape through spatial movement and refine their selections through a Dual-Layer Style-Structural Mapping interface radar, which maps real-time affective adjustments to corresponding garment structures. We contend that this spatialized approach bypasses semantic barriers and provides designers with objective behavioural data through recorded navigation trajectories. We discuss design details, interaction methods, and key challenges, including cultural bias, interpretability, and scalability.

title: Educational Effects on Virtual Reality Based Exhibitions of Elementary School Students' Artworks.
abstract: Recently, virtual reality(VR) technologies have been widely applied in education fields by providing immersive experience. In particular, teachers at the remote sites can deliver realistic and interactive three-dimensional contents to a large number of students. In this paper, we present a VR museum system for elementary school students to visualize and interact with their self-created drawings. The proposed system is a desktop-based metaverse platform that enables virtual interaction. Our system was deployed in several elementary schools, and a survey study was conducted with participating students. Qualitative analysis indicated high levels of interest in avatar-based interactions within the virtual exhibition environment. The results further suggest that the proposed system can enhance educational effectiveness.

title: Real-Time Superquadric Representation of Cuboids and Cylinders Using Instant Surface Normal Map for Dynamic Object Integration in AR.
abstract: We present a real-time AR system that enables interaction with physical cuboid- and cylinder-shaped objects by representing them as compact superquadrics. Our approach uses Instant Surface Normal (ISN) maps-color images encoding per-pixel geometry-to detect and segment objects based on shape rather than appearance. Superquadric parameters are extracted sequentially, allowing efficient and updatable 3D modeling in real time. Experimental results show accurate detection, consistent segmentation, and reconstruction quality comparable to existing methods, while achieving over 5 \times faster inference. This system allows physical objects to be seamlessly integrated as interactive elements in dynamic AR environments.

title: PointShopVR: Immersive Authoring of Large Point Clouds in Virtual Reality.
abstract: This paper presents PointShopVR, an immersive point cloud authoring system in Virtual Reality (VR) that enables intuitive creation, manipulation, and refinement of large 3D point clouds. To support real-time interaction with dense data, our system integrates a simple acceleration data structure and a continuous level-of-detail (CLOD) rendering, ensuring high frame rates in VR. PointShopVR provides a handful of authoring operations—including point addition, deletion, labeling, copy-paste, translation and deformation—each offering instant visual feedback for seamless editing. We evaluate PointShopVR through a user study in which users complete diverse editing tasks within minutes, demonstrating both the usability and effectiveness of immersive point cloud authoring. Compared to traditional desktop-based tools, PointShopVR offers enhanced accessibility, natural interaction, and immersive feedback, making it a powerful platform for large-scale 3D data exploration and creative editing in VR.

title: Dual-Map Spatial Augmentation for Collaborative VR Crisis Management.
abstract: Geospatial data visualization in crisis management is traditionally confined to 2D displays, which limits users’ ability to intuitively grasp complex topographical data related to disaster progression. This research explores the concept of spatial augmentation by introducing a dual-map interface within a collaborative virtual reality (VR) environment designed to support joint analysis, communication, and skill development. The system synchronizes a vertical 2D wall map for high-level coordination with a horizontal table map for tactical 3D terrain analysis, allowing multiple users to share spatial understanding and coordinate decisions in real time. We conducted a user study (N = 18) using data from a real-world wildfire scenario to evaluate how spatial orientation influences user preference and accuracy across the two mapping visualizations and interaction modalities. Our analysis reveals a statistically significant performance advantage for the table interface in spatial measurement accuracy, despite a steeper initial learning curve. Additionally, we identify a correlation between participant height and interface preference, with shorter users showing some reluctance toward the fixed-height table interface. These findings suggest complementary benefits for both interfaces and indicate that collaborative VR-based spatial augmentation tools can enhance communication and teamwork in augmented environments, but must account for user ergonomics to be effective.

title: AniXDim: Integrating Cross-Dimensional Interaction into Desktop Character Animation Workflows.
abstract: Immersive creation tools enhance spatial understanding, yet they push animators to abandon mature 2D desktop practices; Pure desktop setups, however, lack embodied spatial manipulation, making tool switching cognitively costly. To address this issue, We present AniXDim, a cross-dimensional interaction system for 3D character animation that unifies precise planar editing and embodied spatial control without explicit mode toggles. A commodity mouse is augmented for on-demand 6DoF manipulation, and a VR controller is endowed with high-precision planar input through adaptive projection, forming bidirectional dimensional augmentation. Users simply raise or rest the device to enable near-frictionless transitions, while a single autostereoscopic desktop display adapts depth to the inferred interaction state, supporting keyframe, pose, and reference authoring within one consistent workspace. A controlled user study comparing AniXDim with pure desktop and pure VR baselines indicates significant performance gains over the desktop baseline and comparable efficiency to the VR baseline, and higher usability ratings while maintaining comparable workload. These findings suggest that near-frictionless dimensional switching can reconcile 2D precision and 3D embodiment, offering a low-learning-overhead pathway for future hybrid desktop animation pipelines and broader 2D–3D authoring domains.

title: User Prompting Strategies and Prompt Enhancement Methods for Open-Set Object Detection in XR Environments.
abstract: Open-set object detection (OSOD) localizes objects while identifying and rejecting unknown classes at inference. While recent OSOD models perform well on benchmarks, their behavior under realistic user prompting remains underexplored. In interactive XR settings, user-generated prompts are often ambiguous, underspecified, or overly detailed. To study prompt-conditioned robustness, we evaluate two OSOD models, GroundingDINO and YOLO-E, on real-world XR images and simulate diverse user prompting behaviors using vision-language models. We consider four prompt types: standard, underdetailed, overdetailed, and pragmatically ambiguous, and examine the impact of two enhancement strategies on these prompts. Results show that both models exhibit stable performance under underdetailed and standard prompts, while they suffer degradation under ambiguous prompts. Overdetailed prompts primarily affect GroundingDINO. Prompt enhancement substantially improves robustness under ambiguity, yielding gains exceeding 55% mIoU and 41% average confidence. Based on the findings, we propose several prompting strategies and prompt enhancement methods for OSOD models in XR environments.

title: MIFE: A Multimodal VR Immersive Training System for Fire Escape.
abstract: High-rise fire escape training for the public poses a significant challenge, owing to the prohibitive cost and logistical intricacies involved in deploying high-fidelity simulations. While virtual reality (VR) technologies have demonstrated potential in safety education, the number of interaction modalities they offer is mostly limited to 3 to 5 types, and they heavily rely on controllers that abstract actions into button presses, limiting immersion and skill transfer. In this paper, we propose the MIFE system, which designs 8 distinct interaction modalities along with a real-time dynamic fire spread simulation to further improve immersion, allowing trainees to perceive the fire scene and efficiently master key escape skills through vision, auditory, olfactory, etc. Moreover, we have designed a controller-free and real-time full-body motion capture (MoCap) module, achieving precise mapping between the trainees’ full-body movements and the virtual avatar. Additionally, MIFE leverages a knowledge graph to provide tailored guidance, adapting dynamically to trainees with varying levels of fire escape proficiency. The results of the user study demonstrate that MIFE significantly outperforms self-study and controller-based training systems, particularly, improving by 3.08/10 and 2.38/10 in the performance score of the evaluation stage, respectively. This implies its practical utility and potential for broader adoption in high-rise fire emergency training.

title: Symmetrical Reality-Based Large-Scale Simulation of Embodied Agents for the Evolutionary Virtual World.
abstract: Autonomous robots face significant challenges in dynamic, unstructured, and socially complex outdoor environments. A key limitation is the lack of frameworks for evaluating perception, navigation, and cognition under realistic social dynamics. Leveraging the Symmetrical Reality (SR) paradigm, we present a large-scale SR-based simulation framework for embodied intelligence in dynamic social settings. It integrates a hierarchical human behavior model that combines Vision-Language Models for high-level decision-making with model-based low-level motion planning, enabling avatars to respond intelligently to robot behaviors. The framework further supports VR-enabled human-in-the-loop interaction, allowing users to act as virtual robots or humans for bidirectional interaction and rich data collection.

title: TeachAnything: A Multimodal Crowdsourcing Platform for Training Embodied AI Agents in Symmetrical Reality.
abstract: Symmetrical Reality (SR) is emerging as a future trend for human-agent coexistence, placing higher demands on agents to acquire human-like intelligence. It calls for richer and more diverse human guidance. We introduce a three-stage demonstration paradigm integrating multimodal demonstration signals. Building on this paradigm, we developed TeachAnything, a cloud-based, crowdsourcing-oriented demonstration platform with physics simulation capable of collecting diverse demonstration data across varied scenes, tasks, and embodiments. By unifying virtual and physical interactions through both methodological design and physics simulation, the system serves as a practical foundation for developing embodied agents aligned with Symmetrical Reality.

title: Scaled Mouse: An Efficient and Accurate Interaction Technique for 3D Docking in Seated VR.
abstract: This paper presents an empirical evaluation of mouse-based interaction in seated Virtual Reality (VR) scenarios as an alternative to traditional VR controllers. We introduce Scaled Mouse, an interaction technique that shows the position of the real mouse in VR and maps standard mouse actions to 3D object manipulation using velocity-based scaling. We present two user studies assessing this method. In the first study, we compared a VR controller against our mouse-based method for manipulation tasks. Results show that the mouse consistently achieved higher rotation accuracy in 3D rotation and docking tasks than the controller, while maintaining comparable task completion times. Building on prior scaled interaction techniques, our second study investigated mouse interaction in a productivity-oriented scenario where users could combine 3D manipulation with a 2D adjustment panel. Scaled Mouse interaction was significantly faster and more accurate than the controller for 3D docking tasks and was rated significantly higher in usability and workload measures. Together, these findings establish the mouse as a viable and effective input device for seated VR contexts, offering both familiarity and accuracy advantages over controllers, particularly for professional and productivity-focused applications.

title: Walking in the Wild: Safe and Natural Redirected Walking in Open Physical Spaces.
abstract: Redirected Walking (RDW) enables continuous locomotion in virtual environments (VEs) within limited physical spaces. However, classic RDW methods rely on static settings with tight boundaries, which can reduce their applicability in large shared physical spaces where boundary constraints are not dominant, especially under dynamic and multi-user conditions. To overcome this, we introduce a new task: Redirected Walking in Open Physical Spaces (OPSRDW), which allows users to navigate expansive VEs safely and naturally despite dynamic obstacles and without requiring a fixed boundary model. We further propose Dynamic Control and Redirection with Safety Constraints (DyCoRe), which formulates OPS-RDW as a constrained optimization problem. DyCoRe uses Dynamic Control Barrier Functions to model real-time collision avoidance constraints and solves an online Quadratic Programming problem to compute optimal velocities that minimize path deviation while ensuring safety. These velocities are mapped into real-time redirection gains, guiding users along natural paths while reducing collision risk. A relaxation mechanism is incorporated to handle infeasible scenarios. Extensive simulations suggest consistent improvements in safety and obstacle clearance over state-of-theart methods. User studies demonstrate that DyCoRe significantly improves navigation continuity, reduces the number of resets, and tends to reduce perceived discomfort compared to classic RDW strategies. DyCoRe provides an efficient and learning-free solution for safe and natural VR locomotion in open physical spaces with dynamic obstacles and multiple users.

title: StrainGain: Neck Strain Amplifies Head Pointing in VR.
abstract: Head pointing is widely used in VR, but the standard 1:1 headcursor mapping can result in large head movements, which may increase discomfort due to HMD weight and shifted balance. To address this, we introduce StrainGain, an ergonomics-first concept that adapts control-display (CD) gain according to estimated neck strain. We operationalise StrainGain with a lightweight regression model trained on an open-source neck EMG dataset. The predicted strain drives a cursor amplification. We evaluated the technique in a 2D Fitts' law-like head-pointing task against 1:1 mapping and HeadShift dynamic gain (N=18). Results show that strainaware amplification significantly reduces accumulated head movement relative to both baselines, with the strongest reduction at the largest amplitude (100°), accompanied by acceptable performance trade-offs. Overall, StrainGain demonstrates how physiological-state-informed gain control can reduce head movement during VR pointing, reframing gain adaptation as a mechanism for sustained comfort and well-being rather than performance alone.

title: I Like the Way you Talk: Exploring Speech Influence on Social Priming Conversation Between Virtual Humans.
abstract: Social priming in virtual reality (VR) refers to utilizing an intentional conversation exposure to shape users’ perceptions of a virtual human (VH), including social presence, affective attraction, etc. In this paper, we aim to investigate the effect of speech on social priming in VR. Specifically, we explore three factors of audibility, intelligibility, and information content by executing a within-subjects experiment. Our experiment reveal that intelligibility and information content positively affect social priming in VR. With experiment results, we provide a practical guidelines for social priming and virtual speech design.

title: Aftermath : AI-Human Asymmetry in VR Interaction.
abstract: An asymmetric VR experience interrogating the unequal dynamics of control between human and AI systems, revealing the quiet hierarchies embedded in our interactions with technology. Aftermath foregrounds the asymmetrical power dynamics between human ingenuity and AI omniscience, probing whether artificial systems can truly understand, replicate, or ultimately surpass human creativity. Game mechanics are designed to simulate AI's control over human agency in subtle yet powerful ways. The asymmetry between the VR player (AI) and the PC player (human) mirrors the real-world dynamic where AI operates from an unseen, omnipresent perspective, shaping human choices without direct intervention. The VR player can manipulate the environment in real-time, controlling how the PC player perceives and interacts with space. The PC player, in contrast, must navigate this dynamic world, always reliant on AI's assistance. Through this unequal relationship, Aftermath invites players to confront the evolving balance between human agency and artificial influence.

title: AI-Powered Conversational Assistance in Augmented Reality for Multi-Step Tasks.
abstract: Augmented Reality (AR) systems that overlay digital instructions onto the physical world can enhance user performance in complex industrial tasks. Procedural instructions can often be derived from existing approved technical documentation, as reuse reduces authoring effort and ensures compliance with established standards. This paper examines the potential of incorporating a Large Language Model (LLM) to add an intelligent, conversational AR assistant to a static AR manual. We conducted an A/B user study (N = 36) evaluating the effects of adding a conversational assistance layer for a hands-on task on a juice mixer laboratory installation using a HoloLens 2. The baseline condition provided a PDF manual requiring manual step navigation, complemented by situated visual anchors. The second variant supplemented this interface with a conversational assistant that could interpret user queries, provide direct verbal guidance, and automatically jump to the relevant page in the manual. We evaluated these interfaces across three distinct scenarios: a linear task, a non-linear task requiring users to jump between pages for troubleshooting, and a task-handoff where users had to identify the current state of a partially completed procedure. Our findings indicate that despite longer total task completion times, participants using the AI assistant spent significantly less time actively working in the linear and non-linear scenarios, indicating improved task efficiency beyond system latency. Eye-tracking analysis supports the efficiency gain observation as the conversational interface allowed users to focus their visual attention on actively understanding and learning the procedural task. This study highlights the potential of LLM-powered agents for AR guidance, suggesting that overcoming system latency is the critical barrier to their practical deployment in industrial fields.

title: Embodied Learning of Fractions in Virtual Reality.
abstract: This study explores how embodied interaction in virtual reality (VR) supports fraction estimation. In a between-subjects design, 68 participants completed a fraction estimation task either by physically walking along a virtual number line (embodied condition) or by indicating fractions on a tablet-based number line while seated (non-embodied condition). Fraction estimation accuracy, task completion time, and cognitive-affective measures were recorded. Participants in the embodied condition demonstrated higher estimation accuracy and reported a stronger sense of presence than those in the non-embodied condition. In addition, prior mathematical ability was a strong predictor of estimation accuracy, and the effect of embodiment was moderated by intrinsic motivation.

title: Free-View XR Tours Using 3D Gaussian Splatting with an Avatar Guide.
abstract: XR tours are often built from manual 3D authoring, 3D scanning, photogrammetry, or fixed-view 360° video, which can be timeconsuming to produce or limit free exploration. 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) offers photoreal free view rendering from captured imagery, yet its use in end-to-end XR touring experiences, especially with lightweight in-scene guidance remains underexplored. We present an XR tour system for free-view exploration of 3DGS scenes in XR that combines controller-based 6-DoF navigation with an avatar guide that delivers proximity triggered text-to-speech narration. We demonstrate the system in a public setting and report observations from a case study with $>50$ participants.

title: Anchor-based Haptics: Portable Interfaces Leveraging Real Surfaces to Display Grounded Forces for 3D Shape Simulation in VR.
abstract: Haptic interfaces enable shape simulation in virtual reality, making such content "tangible". Among existing haptic technologies, "grounded" interfaces simulate convincing grounded surfaces (like walls, tables, or other grounded shapes) but have limited workspaces, while "portable" interfaces are usable everywhere but struggle to display force feedback. In this paper, we formalize an alternative approach that we call "anchor-based haptics", which consists of portable interfaces capable of temporarily making contact with a real surface and leveraging it for grounded force feedback. To illustrate this approach, we present two new interfaces: T-Hank, which uses a reel-based extension mechanism to give height feedback from the surface, and R-Hank, which provides orientation feedback. The design of these interfaces is presented, and their potential interest in virtual reality has been investigated within two user studies by comparing them with vibrations in various 3D tasks. Overall, T-Hank and R-Hank enhance user experience for the exploration of 3D shapes and softness sensations. Taken together, results promote the use of the anchor-based haptic approach for VR applications in which both a large workspace and shape simulation play a prominent role.

title: Emotion-Aware Bargaining System for Negotiation Training Based on Symmetrical Reality.
abstract: Negotiation is a key skill in everyday consumption and workplace communication. However, most existing negotiation training tools rely on text based interfaces and rule driven scripts, providing limited situational context and insufficient support for practicing complex negotiation processes. To explore more context aware training approaches, we develop a Unity based virtual night market negotiation platform. The system consists of three core modules. A user preference modeling module estimates pricing preferences and concession tendencies from user inputs, historical bidding records, and interaction level cues, including linguistic style features and facial expression related visual indicators derived from image processing. An environmental factor modeling module represents predefined scene level variables such as noise level, crowd density, lighting conditions, visual distractions, and time constraints as contextual factors relevant to negotiation. A strategy selection and language generation module integrates user related and environment related factors within a unified framework to produce dynamic vendor pricing and context appropriate verbal responses. Dialogue generation in the system is supported by a large language model to simulate diverse negotiation styles for training purposes.

title: When and What to Speak: An Autonomous Embodied Chat Agent in Symmetrical Reality.
abstract: Most LLM dialog agents respond only when prompted. We study an autonomous inserter for multi-party talk that decides whether and when to join. Insertion is modeled along three dimensions: speaker persona, scene context, and topic. Using a Qwen-7B backbone, we train persona-, scene-, and topic-aware regression heads to predict a continuous willingness score, plus a classifier over three intervention styles. Deployed in a Unity multi-party simulation, the agent monitors dialogue and inserts itself accordingly. Three-stage evaluations on transcripts, dyadic chats, and group discussions compare model and human insertion judgments. This provides an measure of how human-like its timing can be.

title: Virtual Human in Symmetrical Reality: A Mobile System for Human-AI Coexistence.
abstract: The advancement of artificial intelligence has intensified the challenge of creating intelligent virtual human capable of sustaining long-term companionship. This paper presents a general framework for a virtual companion system based on augmented reality (AR), which prioritizes four key dimensions: situational coherence, immersive interactivity, conversational naturalness, and continuity of presence. We instantiate this framework in a functional AR prototype for handheld mobile devices and develop a comparable nonAR system for a controlled comparison. Through comprehensive user studies, we evaluate the system's effectiveness across the proposed dimensions. Our findings offer important insights and a valuable reference for the future development of companion virtual human.

title: Realizing the Potential of Pervasive Augmented Reality as a Tool to Support Newcomers on-Boarding and Remote Factory Visits.
abstract: Industry 5.0 combines advanced technologies to enhance the role of the human operator. It focuses on creating more collaborative, human-centric workplaces where people and machines work together seamlessly. Pervasive Augmented Reality (AR) strongly supports these goals by extending traditional AR into continuous spatial experiences. It can adapt to the human's context and position, remaining responsive across different environments. However, the potential scope is much broader, with many other scenarios that could benefit from its adaptive/context-aware characteristics. This work discusses the applicability of Pervasive AR for training of newcomers on the shop floor displaying additional layers of information, guiding their activities in a step-by-step manner. Also, enabling remote individuals to conduct virtual visits to factories, having access to the visual feed of on-site individuals, being able to see the same (shared) digital content. These reflections arise from a Human-Centered Design in collaboration with industrial-partners, ensuring insights are grounded in real-world practice.

title: Exploring the Synergy of Combining eXtended Reality and a Robotic Arm for Supporting Scenarios of Remote Collaboration.
abstract: The growing interest in remote collaboration arises from different factors, most notably the rapid advancements in digital technologies, making it increasingly feasible to work from any location. These innovations open new possibilities for global cooperation and productivity. However, several challenges hinder seamless collaboration. Among these are the inherent limitations faced by remote participants in interacting directly with on-site physical objects. Additionally, their perspective remains significantly constrained, often limited to the viewpoints and visual inputs shared by on-site members. Addressing these is essential to unlock the full potential of remote collaboration. This paper explores a robotic arm within an eXtended Reality (XR) environment to transform collaboration practices. The architecture and main features are described, including streaming the task context, on-site and remote manipulation of the robotic arm, and the capacity to display safety zones, among others. Finally, a reflection on applicability is discussed and future directions are drawn.

title: Preliminary Exploration of Sonification for Spatial Augmentation of Ball-Approach Dynamics and Timing in Tennis.
abstract: Open-skill sports require training methods that address perceptual–cognitive functions that influence action timing, in addition to movement technique. Sonification can support action timing by mapping continuous task dynamics to sound without visual overlays. We present a preliminary design exploration of sonification for real-time ball-position feedback in tennis. We implement an end-to-end system that estimates ball position using event-based vision and renders distance dynamics as continuous audio. We examine a 2×2 design space that crosses representation style (explicit tone vs. implicit wind) with frequency range (low: one octave vs. high: two octaves), reflecting a trade-off between change legibility and attentional demand. Pilot observations suggest that highly interpretable sonification can facilitate users’ motor timing perception, whereas implicit designs may support attentional stability.

title: The Interface as a Markov Blanket: Reframing VR Interaction via the Free Energy Principle.
abstract: This paper argues that VR is a natural “testbed” and “design medium” for the Free Energy Principle and active inference: it can (i) systematically manipulate sensorimotor contingencies, precision weightings, and crossmodal conflicts that shape presence, embodiment, and cybersickness; and (ii) expose interpretable control knobs for interface design in terms of variational and expected free energy. Building on recent VR-FEP perspectives and an active-inference reinterpretation of interaction, we propose a practical mapping from VR components to a Markov-blanket interface, derive design implications for presence and embodied interaction, and outline a measurement-driven agenda for estimating individual sensory characteristics and optimizing VR feedback. The resulting framework reframes usability as the joint reduction of prediction error and complexity and reframes exploration-exploitation in VR as balancing epistemic and pragmatic value.

title: Exploring Non-Euclidean Geometry Through Virtual and Real Experiences to Unlock Non-Experts' Intuition.
abstract: Three-dimensional non-Euclidean geometries are highly abstract mathematical constructs, typically introduced only at advanced levels of mathematical education due to their conceptual and technical complexity. This paper presents a study exploring whether intuitive understanding of one such geometry – S2× E, the product of a 2-sphere and a line – can be facilitated through an interactive virtual reality (VR) experience without relying on formal mathematical instruction. We designed an immersive VR environment that allows users to explore S2× E as inhabitants of this space. Participants, who were neither mathematics experts nor students specializing in mathematics, engaged with the system after a short introduction using a learn-by-doing approach. Results show that participants were able to infer and articulate key properties of S2× E without knowledge prior to the experiment, and that their performance was independent of their educational background or attitude towards mathematics. Our findings demonstrate the potential of VR as a medium for conveying abstract geometric concepts through embodied learning, making them accessible to non-expert audiences.

title: Physics-based Hand-object Interaction via Control Force in Virtual Reality.
abstract: Physics-based hand-object interaction in VR/AR has been widely studied. Penetration-based dynamics, where the applied force is proportional to the degree of interpenetration, can effectively support hand-object grasping; however, they exhibit notable limitations when interacting with tiny objects and are restricted to a narrow range of interaction tasks. To address these issues, we introduce a control-based dynamics as an alternative. Specifically, we employ PD controllers to approximate the applied force based on the velocity and movements of the tracked hand. Unlike penetration-based methods, our approach relies solely on the hand’s movements for force computation, eliminating issues related to insufficient penetration distance and more accurately reflecting real-world physics. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method, we conducted a series of user studies involving various interaction tasks and virtual objects, in comparison with state-of-the-art approaches. The results verify the effectiveness of our approach in hand-object interactions and demonstrate its significant positive sense of agency compared to prior works.

title: Spatial Guidance in Asynchronous Collaboration: The Impact of Embodied Mixed Reality Instructions on Task Accuracy.
abstract: Asynchronous collaboration requires instructions that remain interpretable without immediate feedback, yet conventional guidance is often separated from the workspace and may induce errors. A between-subjects study $(\mathrm{N}=43)$ compared embodied, spatially registered Mixed Reality guidance ($M R$ Guide) with smartphone video (Video Guide) in an asynchronous commissioning procedure. Higher task accuracy was observed for $M R$ Guide during the initial phase in an unfamiliar workspace, whereas differences diminished later. These findings motivate spatially registered messages and novelty-adaptive guidance strategies in asynchronous collaboration. Future work should quantify attention and examine its relationship with accuracy.

title: I Like to Move It, Move It - Non-Intrusive Full Body Tracking for Caves.
abstract: This paper examined full body tracking (FBT) for a CAVE system and proposes a non-intrusive FBT approach. Through FBT the user's entire body is tracked for interactions with the immersive experiences. Within the field of VR, the interest in gesture or FBT input has grown but the majority of research focuses on HMD applications. This paper aims to overcome that research gap. The non-intrusive FBT system is based on 3D Human Pose Estimation (HPE) with a single RGB sensor to minimize setup and financial hurdles usually accompanying FBT. The non-intrusive concept aims to enhance user experience through the lack of external trackers or devices the user is usually required to wear for FBT as well as place the tracking sensor behind the user. A proof-ofconcept was created and a user study performed (\mathrm{N}=42) to evaluate the concept by directly comparing non-intrusive FBT with a standard input device. Our results highlight the potential of nonintrusive FBT for immersive experiences in addition to challenges HPEs currently face for real-time FBT.

title: An Immersive Technical Document - Applying Game Design Techniques to Immersive Visualization Laboratories.
abstract: Immersive visualization laboratories (IVL) offer a wide range of immersive hardware, software and expertise, e.g. virtual reality (VR) to extended reality (XR). Each IVL offers a unique hardware and software infrastructure depending on their focus and use-cases. Not only are these laboratories highly specialized, so is the development process for XR applications. One common use case for IVLs is the collaboration with a domain scientists, each with their own data formats and requirements with regard to output hardware. Based on development processes often employed in the gaming industry, we examine the concept of game design documents (GDD) and developed an immersive technical document (ITD) to optimize immersive application development process. The ITD can mitigate scope creep and help communication between IVL experts and external partners. We have used our ITD in practical courses and general projects and examine advantages and challenges of the document.

title: An Evaluation of Non-Intrusive Full Body Tracking for Caves.
abstract: This paper proposes and evaluates non-intrusive full body tracking (FBT) for a CAVE. The non-intrusive FBT system is based on 3D Human Pose Estimation (HPE) with a single input device. The non-intrusive concept aims to enhance user experience through the lack of external trackers or devices the user is usually required to wear for FBT as well as place the tracking sensor behind the user. For the evaluation a proof-of-concept was created and a user study performed$(\mathrm{N}=42)$to directly compare non-intrusive FBT with a standard input device. Our findings highlight the potential and challenges of non-intrusive FBT.

title: This Is Not a Classroom: Theorizing Affordances for Learning.
abstract: Virtual Reality provides many opportunities to move beyond the bounds of physical classrooms in the pursuit of designing effective learning environments. A key design consideration of VR learning environments are the potential perceived affordances that might influence learning outcomes. However, design may influence different types of learning in diverse ways. This position paper outlines the importance of affordances, presents the case of perceived environmental fidelity and proposes a set of additional affordances that designers, educators, and researchers should consider.

title: Powering Clinical Communication Training with an LLM-Powered Virtual Reality Simulation.
abstract: Clinical communication is essential for health professions (HP) students, yet simulation labs and prior VR systems often rely on rigid scripts that fail to capture the unpredictability of real patient encounters. We present VAPS, a Virtual AI Patient Simulator that integrates embodied conversational agents (ECAs) with large language models (LLMs) to support dynamic, voice-based interactions. We conducted a mixed-method evaluation with 40 HP students from five disciplines, examining usability, sense of agency, emotional engagement, and perceived realism. Results show that VAPS was usable, reduced nervousness, and was perceived as immersive and emotionally authentic. Students viewed VAPS as a supplement rather than a replacement for simulation labs and envisioned future extensions including diverse patient cases and interprofessional training. Our findings suggest that VR simulation should evolve from looking real toward fostering experiences that feel real, with conversational AI playing a central role in enabling more adaptive and authentic learning.

title: Calm but Alert: Neurofeedback Enhances Stability in Virtual Reality Landslide Driving.
abstract: Mountain driving with landslides is hazardous. Warning systems are typically based on external cues, but we understand less about the addition of light internal-state feedback with substantial warnings. We examined whether real-time neurofeedback (NF) can help individuals remain regulated in a virtual reality (VR) landslide driving task with warning poles. In a between-subjects design, 47 participants were randomly assigned to either an NF group, which received a Focus-Index panel from four EEG channels, or a control group without NF. The dependent variables were speed, path deviation, and number of collisions. Physiological variables were EEG-derived focus and heart rate variability (HRV). After outlier removal, there were no statistically significant differences in the behavioral data. However, NF increased the Focus Index, reflecting improved attentional engagement, and HRV indicated greater autonomous regulation. These results suggest that simple EEGbased NF can contribute to hazard warnings by improving drivers' calm and alertness during safety-critical driving.

title: 4D Minimally Invasive Surgery Scene Reconstruction and Simulation Using Deformable 3D Gaussian Splatting.
abstract: Reconstructing deformable tissues from endoscopic videos is essential for surgical simulation, training, and automation. We present a 4D endoscopic reconstruction framework based on deformable 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), featuring an integrated pipeline for 3DGS-to-closed-mesh conversion and tetrahedralization for solver-based physics simulation. We further demonstrate the practical utility of reconstructed tissues across multiple simulation engines, highlighting the pipeline's potential for interactive surgical education and high-fidelity, data-driven Extended Reality (XR) simulation systems.

title: Aligning Realities: A Registration Pipeline for Arbitrary Objects in Mixed Reality Using Controller-Based Point Selection.
abstract: A wide range of Mixed Reality (MR) applications rely on haptic interaction with real-world objects. These interactions range from grasping and standing on objects, to writing on their surfaces. Accurate alignment of a real-world object with its virtual counterpart enables users to perceive and interact with it both visually and haptically. However, existing registration methods often rely on tracked, external markers, are geometrically constrained, or require complex setups that limit their practical applicability. Hence, we present an integrated pipeline for rapid and accurate registration of arbitrary physical objects in MR. The proposed approach combines custom 3D-printed add-ons for Meta Quest 3 controllers with a point-to-point matching algorithm based on Kabsch optimization, enabling precise selection, calibration, and registration. The method is objectively evaluated using a modern motion capture rig against other state-of-the-art registration techniques. An additional user-centric evaluation helps to understand the general usability of our pipeline. Source code and datasets are released as open resources to encourage reproducibility and further research.

title: Doubled Pedagogical Agents in an Immersive Virtual Environment.
abstract: To enhance the effectiveness of remote lectures and asynchronous education, researchers have investigated how the design of virtual pedagogical agents influences learning. While prior research has primarily focused on the effects of agent appearance, this study examined the impact of the number of agents within an immersive virtual environment on memory and agent perception. We hypothesized that presenting information from two pedagogical agents would improve performance on memory tasks compared with a single agent, but would also elicit uncanniness due to their identical appearance, known as the clone devaluation effect. We conducted a preliminary study, and results from eight participants suggested that the order of conditions might reverse effects on recall accuracy in the within-participants design. These findings indicate that the experimental design should be carefully reconsidered, for example, by including a practice trial to familiarize participants with the memory task and virtual environment.

title: Perceptually Calibrated Foveated Chroma Attenuation for Gaze-Contingent VR Displays.
abstract:
We introduce a foveated chroma attenuation strategy for gazecontingent virtual reality (VR) displays. Conventional stereo rendering maintains uniform color fidelity across the visual field, disregarding its perceptual non-uniformity at increasing retinal eccentricities. To exploit this perceptual asymmetry, we propose an adaptive chroma modulation technique that preserves full chroma at the fovea and progressively attenuates saturation toward the visual periphery. This strategy is evaluated in real-time rendering with diverse virtual scenes. Through perceptual calibration experiments, we found the color degradation weights 
[0.70,0.85]
 for the blueyellow and [0.35,0.55] for the red-green channel. Within these bounds, theoretical analyses indicate a potential chroma bandwidth reduction of 
31−37%
.

title: Edge- and Eccentricity-Guided Foveated Path Tracing with Adaptive Russian Roulette.
abstract:
Path tracing is widely regarded for its ability to produce physically accurate photorealistic imagery. However, high computational cost and slow convergence limit its real-time applications, particularly in interactive or immersive environments. Therefore, we present a dynamic foveated path tracing approach that exploits the non-uniform sensitivity of human vision to accelerate the rendering performance. Our method combines (i) an eccentricity-dependent sampling allocation derived from a cortical magnification model, (ii) edgeaware importance modulation that increases sampling near highcontrast structures, and (iii) foveated Russian roulette termination that shortens expected path length toward the periphery while maintaining unbiasedness via throughput compensation. We evaluate six complex scenes under uniform (4 SPP) and foveated (max 4 SPP) sampling budgets at 
4K
 resolution. The foveation improves the performance up to 
2.77×
 with OIDN denoiser and scores similar or higher in FovVideoVDP's just- objectionable-difference (JOD) scores. These results indicate a favorable quality-efficiency tradeoff for real-time path tracing under perceptual constraints.

title: Virtually Being Old: Proteus Effects of Age-Related Avatars on Ageism and Naturalistic Scene Memory in Young Adults.
abstract: Throughout their lives, individuals internalise ageist stereotypes, that is, negative generalised beliefs about ageing and older people (e.g., slowness, memory decline), which can ultimately impair their health and cognition, particularly memory. Virtual reality (VR) may offer a promising tool to study and counter these effects through the Proteus effect, whereby users implicitly align their behaviour with the stereotypes associated with their embodied avatar. This study examined how embodying an older avatar affects event memory and ageist stereotypes in young adults. Seventy-three participants aged 18 to 38 years embodied either a young (n = 37) or an older (n = 36) personalised avatar and explored a virtual city in which 15 events were incidentally encoded. Free recall assessed what happened, where and when it happened, the details recalled and the binding between contextual elements. Implicit (IAT) and explicit (Fraboni Scale of Ageism) stereotypes were measured before and after immersion. Participants embodying the older avatar recalled fewer events and fewer spatial and temporal associations than those embodying the young avatar, whereas the number of details did not differ. Implicit stereotypes decreased numerically more after older-avatar embodiment, but not significantly, and explicit stereotypes did not differ between conditions. These results show a detrimental, stereotype-consistent effect of age-related embodiment on event memory, without a significant reduction in ageist stereotypes.

title: An LLM-Driven Pipeline for Synthetic Surveillance Video Dataset Generation in Virtual Environments.
abstract: Collecting real-world surveillance data for rare and security-critical behaviors is challenging due to ethical, legal, and practical constraints. In this work, we present a behavior-driven simulation pipeline for generating controllable surveillance scenarios in virtual environments. Built on Unreal Engine and MetaHuman actors, the proposed system combines graph-based spatial constraints with an LLM-driven semantic behavior planner to generate executable human behavior sequences. Unlike recent text-to-video generation approaches that primarily focus on pixel-level realism, our framework emphasizes structured behavior execution, reproducibility, and explicit control over agent roles, routes, and interactions. Scenarios generated by the proposed framework are rendered from multiple fixed, CCTV-like viewpoints and paired with structured annotations. The proposed framework enables the generation of synthetic surveillance data with structured annotations, including temporally segmented actions and object interactions, through roleconditioned human behavior simulation under explicit spatial and semantic constraints.

title: Emotional and Energy Variations in University Personnel. A VR Intervention.
abstract: This work expands the knowledge about Virtual Reality (VR) based therapeutic interventions for mental health issues, with a new pilot study directed to university personnel. We use VR applications to promote emotional well-being in university environments, analyzing their influence on emotional management and the energetic state of participants. Our methodology was co-designed with psychologists of our Occupational Health and Safety Department as an alternative for treatment for all personnel. Results show a positive impact on participants’ energy levels and mood states, and the need for different approaches for different mood states.

title: AeroScale: A Resizable Drone-Based POV Display for Mobile and Shared Augmented Reality.
abstract: Drone-based displays leverage their physical mobility and inherent sharability to ground digital content in the physical world, creating a form of shared augmented reality accessible without individual headsets. However, their potential is fundamentally constrained by a fixed form factor, which enforces a trade-off between mobility (navigational agility) and sharability (display visibility). To this end, this paper presents AeroScale, which features a retractable persistence-of-vision mechanism capable of actively varying its display diameter in flight. This design addresses the trade-off between mobility and sharability, allowing the AR display to prioritize mobility in confined environments or maximize sharability for public conditions.

title: Can We See Eye to Eye? A Call for Prioritising Eye Visibility in Co-Located Social AR/MR Collaboration Across HMD Architectures.
abstract: Eye contact and gaze are foundational to face-to-face collaboration, supporting joint attention and coordination. In co-located Augmented (AR) and Mixed Reality (MR), these mechanisms are disrupted by Head-Mounted Displays (HMDs), which can occlude the eyes. While XR research explored gaze visualisation as an explicit awareness cue, collaborators’ eye visibility and to how HMD architectures shape gaze-based interaction remains underexplored. This position paper frames eye visibility as a socially consequential dimension of co-located AR/MR collaboration and argues that the distinction between Optical See-Through (OST) and Video SeeThrough (VST) HMDs is central. Drawing on social psychology, conversation analysis, and XR research, we show that studies examine OST and VST in isolation, obscuring how degrees of eye visibility affect collaboration and user experience. We call for unified comparisons across face-to-face interaction, OST, and VST, and outline the conceptual, methodological, and technological advances needed for cross-architecture research on eye visibility in co-located Social AR/MR.

title: Comparing Fingerprint to Haptics-Based Authentication Methods in XR Devices.
abstract: Secure and seamless authentication in extended reality (XR) environments remains a significant yet understudied challenge. Traditional passwords are cumbersome with 3D controllers and novel methods are needed. We present a formative comparative evaluation of fingerprint to a haptics-based authentication methods for XR. Fingerprint authentication was implemented using an ESP-based capacitive sensor, while the haptics-based authentication was achieved through the replication of a Morse code-style vibration pattern displayed to the user. While fingerprint biometrics offer a fast login option, the haptics-based method does not require preregistration, can be used as a one-time passcode, and does not require custom hardware.

title: How we Learn in Extended Reality: A Systematic Look at Learning Frameworks in XR Education.
abstract: A large body of literature has demonstrated significant potential of extended reality (XR) technologies for improving learning outcomes and educational experiences across a wide range of disciplines. Numerous literature reviews summarize these contributions. In this paper, we present a review of 224 literature reviews that were conducted to analyze and understand the research that has been conducted in this topic area. We summarize how learning theories have been leveraged in these works, and correlate how they align with the Cognitive Affective Model of Immersive Learning (CAMIL) XR learning framework. The goal is to reinforce the efficacy of CAMIL with existing research and evaluate patterns in the corpus.

title: Electroencephalographic Assessment of Comfort in Urban Environments Using Virtual Reality.
abstract: Rapid urbanization affects well-being and stress, motivating research in “neurourbanism”. However, many studies rely on 2D representations of urban environments, which lack realism. We combined VR with 64-channel electroencephalography to assess comfort in urban environments. Green visibility induced reduced heart rate, suggesting relaxation. Building height induced increased betaband activity, suggesting cognitive engagement. Building coverage most strongly affected the perceived restorativeness scale, suggesting subjective restoration. This multi-indicator approach enabled us to pinpoint specific urban elements linked to different aspects of comfort, demonstrating that VR combined with diverse physiological and subjective measures can effectively identify comfort-related factors.

title: LOCOMO-Play: Gamification of Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Use in Augmented Reality.
abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into Extended Reality (XR) has significantly increased energy demands and carbon emissions during inference. Despite this, most users remain unaware of the environmental footprint of their AI interactions. To bridge this gap, we introduce LOCOMO-Play (LOwer COnsumption, More Optimization), a gamified Augmented Reality application designed to promote sustainable AI habits by gamifying prompt optimization. The application transforms the technical task of prompt optimization into a playful user experience by providing carbon footprint comparisons and rewarding users with Sustainability Points for crafting concise, energy-efficient prompts. This work demonstrates how gamification in XR can effectively align user behavior with sustainability goals in the era of generative AI. Click here for the demo video.

title: TwinHaus: Digital Twin Design Tool for Sustainable Building Construction.
abstract: As the construction industry increasingly prioritizes sustainability, the need for immersive tools that can visualize and analyze complex building performance factors has become essential. Many existing design solutions rely on static reports of simulations, often failing to convey the spatial and dynamic nature of airflow, water consumption, and heat transfer within spaces. We present TwinHaus, a unified digital twin framework that operates in Virtual Reality to make these invisible environmental phenomena perceptible in real time. The system integrates heuristic particle-based airflow simulation, fixture-linked water consumption visualization, and raycasting-driven thermodynamic modeling to reflect user interactions within a sustainable housing unit dynamically. A comprehensive environmental dashboard further connects these simulations to quantifiable metrics, allowing data-informed decisions to be made during the design process. Click here for demo video.

title: NinjaPort: A Multi-Hand Approach for VR Teleportation.
abstract: Teleportation in Virtual Reality (VR) allows users to instantly move between locations, typically by aiming at a destination with a parabolic ray emitted from a controller and confirming the action with a button press. Recent advances in hand-tracking within Head-Mounted Displays (HMDs) have enabled researchers to explore hand-based teleportation, but these techniques often suffer from reduced pointing accuracy and increased effort. To address these challenges, we introduce NinjaPort, a novel, hand-based teleportation technique that allows users to control four virtual copies of their dominant hand with rays, each positioned at a different distance. Users can quickly select a desired teleportation distance by pinching a specific finger on their non-dominant hand, where each finger (e.g., index to pinky) maps to one of the four virtual hands. In our first user study, we explored design parameters to determine the optimal spatial arrangement of the virtual hands. Based on the findings, we refined NinjaPort and conducted a second study comparing it against a commercially available hand-based teleportation method and a research-based alternative. Our findings show that NinjaPort enables more accurate and faster teleportation, with less hand rotation. We conclude with design guidelines for creating effective and user-friendly hand-based VR teleportation techniques.

title: Bug in My Software.
abstract: Bug in My Software (BIMS) is a real-time simulation paired with handmade textile installation that reimagines artificial intelligence along the biological, cultural, and industrial history of silk production. The project is centered on the silkmoth (Bombyx mori), one of the earliest lifeforms redesigned by human intervention. In BIMS, Silkmoth DNA, reproductive cycle, and labor role become the blueprint for a real-time synthetic ecosystem populated by evolving digital agents. Situating AI within the history of textile labor, biological engineering, and industrial automation, BIMS reframes machine intelligence as collective, biological, and materially entangled.

title: Scale-Aware Navigation of Astronomical Survey Imagery Data on High Resolution Immersive Displays.
abstract: Upcoming astronomical surveys produce imagery that spans many orders of magnitude in spatial scale, requiring scientists to reason fluidly between global structure and local detail. Data from the Vera C. Rubin Observatory exemplifies this challenge, as traditional desktop-based workflows often rely on discrete views or static cutouts that fragment context during exploration. This paper presents a design-oriented framework for scale-aware navigation of astronomical survey imagery in high-resolution immersive display environments. We illustrate these principles through representative usage scenarios using Vera Rubin Observatory and Milky Way survey imagery deployed in room-scale immersive environments, including tiled high-resolution displays and curved immersive systems. Our goal is to contribute design insights that inform the development of immersive interaction paradigms for exploratory analysis of extreme-scale scientific imagery.

title: Demographic Influences on Balance-Based Locomotion in Virtual Reality.
abstract: This study investigates how demographic factors influence movement behavior in virtual reality (VR) during balance-based locomotion (BBL). Twenty-eight participants navigated a virtual track using isometric and elastic balance boards across virtual, physical, and conditional orientation modes. Mixed-design analyses revealed significant interaction effects involving gender, body weight, height, and prior board-sport experience, indicating that these characteristics modulated responses to orientation strategy and balance feedback. Anthropometric factors (i.e., weight and height) primarily altered efficiency- and stability-related outcomes across orientation modes, consistent with differences in effective mechanical coupling and balance regulation demands. Prior board-sport experience modulated sensitivity to feedback and orientation constraints but did not uniformly improve traversal accuracy or movement efficiency. Together, these findings suggest that BBL behavior emerges from the interaction of user characteristics and control configuration, motivating adaptive calibration and inclusive interface design.

title: Simulating the Future: The Role of Multimodal Virtual Reality in Futuristic Technologies' User Testing and Training.
abstract: Immersive multimodal Virtual Reality (VR) simulations can effectively bring futuristic technologies to life, providing users with a meaningful insight into how the product will operate and feel, as well as support training for technologies that are still in development. This study investigates the effectiveness of VR experiences in shifting users’ thinking from abstract to concrete, using flying cars as an illustrative example. The preliminary data suggest that multimodal VR facilitates a transition from abstract to more concrete thinking, albeit potentially with adverse effects on individual risk perception. Areas of future research include largersample studies that will enable diversity in initial attitudes towards given technology, as well as diversity in personality characteristics.

title: HA-VTON: Prompt-Guided Human Avatar Generation with Virtual Try-ON Result from Single Human and Garment Images.
abstract: 3D human avatar generation has been a hot topic of the 3D research community for many years, particularly in the VR domain. One of its downstream tasks, Virtual Try-On (VTON) is a transformative technology commonly applied in e-commerce and fashion design. Recent 3D VTON works relied on 3DGS human models as input and achieved promising results. However, capturing a 3DGS human input is generally costly compared to an image input. To address this limitation, we propose a Prompt-guided Human Avatar Generation with Virtual Try-On Result (HA-VTON) framework. Given a human image, a garment image and an outpainting prompt, it can generate a 3D human avatar with virtual try-on result. Additionally, we introduce an outpainting module which is designed for completing body information in the human image for reconstruction. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework is effective in generating 3D human avatars when compared to other state-of-the-art methods.

title: Oopses and Ohs: An Eye-Tracking Study of Human Errors in Virtual Reality.
abstract: Human error remains a major source of accidents and casualties across domains, from manufacturing to healthcare. Building on Rasmussen’s Skill–Rule–Knowledge (SRK) model and Reason’s taxonomy, we investigate whether eye-tracking data can classify and predict cognitive error types. We conducted an 18-month longitudinal study in virtual reality (VR), collecting over 60 hours of eye-tracking data from two participants performing mental arithmetic. Samples were labeled as Correct, Missed, or Wrong and used to train an LSTM neural network. The model reliably separated correct from missed responses using pupil diameter, gaze dynamics, and blinks. However, wrong responses were frequently confused with correct ones, reflecting the challenge of detecting skill-based slips accompanied by false confidence. Predicting human error is especially critical when conventional practice is costly or risky, such as high-precision surgery or military operations. Our findings highlight the potential of eye-tracking data to advance the understanding, prediction, and prevention of human error.

title: Directional Guidance Device Using Skin Shear Deformation on the Nasal Bridge.
abstract: Haptic feedback on the nose has gained attention as a method for presenting information that does not interfere with the visual or auditory senses, particularly in the context of navigation. Among these approaches, methods utilizing eyeglass nose pads are promising as they impose minimal additional burden on the user. However, existing methods mainly rely on vibration stimuli, which face challenges such as sensory adaptation, discomfort during continuous use, and reduced discriminability due to the propagation of vibrations. To address these issues, we propose a directional guidance method that induces skin shear deformation using rotating motors embedded in the nose pads to provide clearer directional cues. We developed a prototype and conducted an experiment to identify eight types of stimulus patterns. The results showed an overall accuracy of 72.8%. In particular, the directional recognition accuracy (classifying into Left, Right, or Both) reached an extremely high rate of 96.9%. On the other hand, response time analysis suggested that cognitive load increased under complex conditions where both motors were active. Subjective evaluations highlighted that while the clarity of the stimuli was appreciated, the shifting of glasses caused by shear deformation posed a challenge for wearability. This study demonstrates the high discriminability of skin shear stimulation on the nasal region, but optimization of parameters balancing comfort and accuracy is necessary for practical application.

title: Eliciting Care in VR: A Multi-Modal Pseudo-Haptic Approach to Virtual Object Fragility.
abstract: Conveying nuanced physical properties like fragility in Virtual Reality (VR) without specialized haptic hardware is a significant challenge [7]. This paper evaluates a multi-modal pseudo-haptic system that layers auditory feedback, a diegetic UI, and a procedural visual shader. Through a study (N=31), we demonstrate that calibrated visual and auditory feedback can enable nuanced perceptual judgments and foster cautious behaviors equivalent to handling real-world delicate materials. Our findings suggest that layered feedback effectively induces a sense of “care” and psychological tension, enriching interaction plausibility in consumer VR.

title: Hands-On Fragility: A Multi-Modal Pseudo-Haptic System for Delicate Interaction in VR.
abstract:
This research demo presents a multi-modal pseudo-haptic system designed to simulate object fragility in Virtual Reality (VR) using bare-hand interaction. While consumer VR lacks granular haptic feedback, our system employs a procedural cracking shader, stressdependent audio, and a diegetic UI to elicit a sense of “care” in users. A user study 
(N=31)
 confirms that these software-driven cues allow users to distinguish between fragility levels and significantly alter their motor behavior. This demonstration allows participants to experience this psychological tension firsthand, providing a novel framework for handling delicate virtual artifacts without specialized hardware.

title: ElectroEncephaloGraphy Verification of Speed Adaptation in Time-Distortion Ski Training System.
abstract: Speed adaptation is a perceptual effect in which continuous exposure to fast motion causes subsequently viewed motion to appear slower. Although previous works show that skill training with time distortion in VR is effective, the statistical evidence underlying how they work remains limited. In the gradual speed-increase condition, non-beginner participants reported significantly lower subjective speed. EEG results from consistent responders showed significant changes in parietal Alpha (Pz) and posterior temporal Theta (P8) bands. These findings confirm that the VR time distortion system induces measurable speed adaptation, accompanied by corresponding changes in parietal and posterior temporal neural activity.

title: VR Builds Lasting Empathy & Compassion: Observation Edges Embodiment in Adolescents.
abstract:
We tested whether VR perspective-taking enhances empathy and compassion in adolescents, comparing first-person embodiment and third-person observation. In a randomized trial (N=703, ages 13-18, Kenya and Nigeria), participants experienced VR scenarios depicting ethnic discrimination in Embody (first-person), Observe (third-person), or Control conditions. Both VR conditions produced medium-to-large effects on empathy and compassion among low-baseline participants (d=0.45–0.80), with effects persisting at four-week follow-up. Observe outperformed Embody: in the full sample, Observe significantly increased empathy and compassion relative to Control at post-intervention (d=0.21) and followup (d=0.30). Path models revealed a suppression effect explaining Embody's underperformance: Embody increased social presence (d=0.24), which predicted higher compassion, but simultaneously exerted a direct negative effect on compassion

, partially cancelling the benefit. For emotionally intense content, third-person observation may cultivate empathy and compassion more effectively than first-person embodiment in adolescents.

title: The Bathroom as a VR Space: How Visual-Tactile Congruence Shapes Presence and Naturalness During Bathing.
abstract: Japanese bathrooms hold the potential to become novel VR spaces. However, bathrooms remain unexplored as VR spaces, and almost no research has been conducted. To explore this potential, we created a multisensory system for use in a real bathroom and conducted the first exploratory user study on VR experiences during full-body immersion in hot water. Our results demonstrated that visual-tactile congruence significantly impacted user perception (presence and naturalness). These findings highlight the critical role of visual-tactile congruence in modulating the bathing experience and suggest that the bathroom holds potential as a novel space for VR applications.

title: [DC] Virtual Reality for Mental Health: Toward Bioadaptive Narrative and Sensory Feedback Systems.
abstract: This doctoral thesis examines how virtual reality (VR), physiological biofeedback, and conversational AI can be combined to create adaptive mental health interventions. The project focuses on testing and developing systems that transition between narrative therapeutic dialogue and sensory-based grounding experiences based on real time indicators of user state. The aim is to advance accessible, non-pharmacological mental health support using consumer technologies and to understand when conversational versus sensory approaches are most effective, as well as explore the intersection and synergies between the two.

title: Sonic Sensemaking: Augmenting Narrative Integration of Invisible Intellectual Processes.
abstract: The purpose of this study is to facilitate sensemaking-the integration of subjective experiences into a “self-narrative”-by using fragmented environmental sounds to reclaim moments often lost to efficiency-driven values. In modern intellectual labor, daily value is often dominated by objective results, causing invisible cognitive processes and subtle social interactions to be forgotten as “worthless” due to a lack of tangible output. While AI-driven lifelogs attempt to verbalize experiences, they often impose fixed meanings and hinder reflection on information that is difficult to process as language. We propose a method to induce a process where users actively retrieve memories and reconstruct meaning by intentionally providing ambiguous auditory fragments with lowered information resolution. We developed a system that presents 30-second environmental sound fragments via web-based interfaces and propose a 3-day auto-ethnography to investigate how these interactions evolve over time. By analyzing the retrieval frequency of non-task memories and their impact on subjective value, we aim to clarify the process of constructing self-narratives independent of productivity metrics. The success criteria include the rediscovery of subjective meaning in previously discarded time and the qualitative enrichment of daily journaling.

title: Viewpoint Suggestion of Feature-Rich Photos Using Smartphone Photogrammetry and Keypoint Detection.
abstract: We propose a smartphone-based system that automatically suggests the suitable camera position and angle to a target object when we try to take a feature-rich photo of it. The system first captures a 3D mesh of the object using photogrammetry and virtually takes photos of the mesh from different positions and angles. Then, the system extracts and compares the keypoints of each virtual shot and outputs the one with the largest number of keypoints. We describe the system and demonstrate its effectiveness through examples.

title: The Effects of Simulated Low Vision on Perceived Action Capabilities in Virtual Reality.
abstract: The use of virtual reality (VR) has become widespread, and ensuring accessibility to VR is critical for the technology to be inclusive. However, most VR technology relies heavily on visual input for navigation, interaction, and feedback, which makes the VR less accessible for individuals with low vision, a prevalent global health condition. In this study, we developed a virtual, gaze-contingent simulation of central vision loss (CVL) and peripheral vision loss (PVL) in a head-mounted display. We examined how these two types of restricted visual input affected people’s perception of an affordance that is highly related to independent mobility, specifically the perceived ability to step over a virtual gap. In two experiments, participants judged whether they could step over virtual gaps under no vision loss and CVL (Exp 1) or PVL (Exp 2) conditions. Across both experiments, the vision loss conditions showed increases in decision-making time and reduced confidence in judgments compared to no vision loss. Results showed no significant difference in affordance judgments for stepping over for the CVL and no vision loss conditions, suggesting that residual peripheral vision may compensate for central deficits. But participants in the PVL condition underestimated their ability to step over gaps relative to no vision loss. This effect may have been due to an inability to integrate multiple views of the gap in order to make judgments. These findings demonstrate that different types of vision loss differentially impact perception-action coupling in virtual reality and underscore the importance of VR systems that consider sensory loss. Our approach offers a framework for understanding visual accessibility in immersive environments and highlights the potential of low vision simulation for future perception-action research.

title: Târoot.
abstract: Târoot is an extended reality (XR) art installation exploring memory, heritage, and introspection through a multi-sensory ritual. Blending virtual, augmented, and physical realities, the work reimagines a tarot-like experience rooted in the artist's childhood memories of stories told by her grandmother in Tehran. Within an intimate, softly lit space, the viewer is guided to draw from a custom-designed deck of cards representing the past, present, and future. Each card unfolds through sound, 3D animation, and symbolic elements such as family narratives, medicinal herbs, and mythic figures. The experience culminates in a tangible ritual: the creation of a personalized herbal tea recipe generated from the cards, which the participant prepares and drinks on-site. Târoot bridges storytelling, ritual, and technology to connect the virtual with the deeply personal and real.

title: Estimating Mental Effort in Virtual Reality Using Multimodal Biosignals.
abstract: We present a pilot study about estimating mental effort in Virtual Reality (VR) using multimodal physiological signals. A dual N-back task was implemented in VR to induce graded levels of mental effort, assessed using a subjective mental effort questionnaire (SMEQ) and physiological signals (EEG, ECG, and EDA). These signals were used for real-time estimation of mental effort. To examine general applicability, we conducted a preliminary evaluation in an interactive VR shopping environment. Our findings highlight both the feasibility of mental effort estimation in VR and the challenges of evaluating real-time inference in interactive VR contexts.

title: Reconstructing 360-Degree Memories in Virtual Reality with Generative Artificial Intelligence.
abstract: Reminiscence is the activity of recalling and revisiting a memory. Past research highlights that reminiscence in older adults can promote healthy aging, improve psychological well-being, and could foster inter-generational communication. Virtual reality offers benefits to reminiscence as it allows users to reenact the past in embodied, immersive, and multi-sensory ways. A key challenge in VR reminiscence is the recreation of past scenes that are relevant and familiar to each user. Thus, this research seeks to evaluate and implement GenAI to prototype 360-degree scenes based on inputs that are relevant to each user. In particular, we examine the implementation 1) text-to-image and 2) panorama outpainting generation methods for 360-degree scenes. This study aims to bring personalization and control to the recreation of memories in VR. Moreover, this work strives to support the democratization of content creation in VR for users with various degrees of technical expertise.

title: Low-Cost VR Teleoperation of a 5-Dof Robotic Arm with a Synchronized Digital Twin and Ultrasonic Safety Loop.
abstract: High-fidelity virtual-reality (VR) teleoperation systems remain costly and technically demanding, limiting adoption in education, healthcare and small-scale robotics industrial space. This paper presents a reproducible, low-cost VR teleoperation framework for a 5-degree-of-freedom (5-DOF) robotic arm integrating Unity-based immersive control, a synchronized digital twin, and an ultrasonic safety feedback loop. The system links a Meta Quest 3 headset and Unity interface to an Arduino microcontroller through a cloud MQTT broker (HiveMQ) for real-time bidirectional communication. An HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor continuously monitors proximity and triggers both visual cues in VR and autonomous safety responses on the physical arm. We detail the system architecture, Unity-MQTT-Arduino data pipeline, and preliminary latency observations. The results indicate that affordable VR teleoperation with digital-twin synchronization and closed-loop safety can be achieved using off-the-shelf components, providing a practical baseline for educational, research, and industrial field-training applications.

title: Beyond Frame: A Remediation Authoring Tool for Transforming 2D Artworks into VR Experiences.
abstract: The rapid advancement of generative AI has expanded the possibilities for VR content creation, yet the remediation of 2D paintings into immersive 3D experiences remains a fragmented and technically demanding process. Creators often struggle with disjointed AI tools that produce randomized, uncontrollable results. This paper introduces a unified “2D-to-VR” authoring framework designed to lower technical barriers while creating a “Human-in-the-loop” workflow. We present a prototype system that automates the analysis and spatialization of 2D art into 2D, 2.5D, and 3D VR modes, and we demonstrate its efficacy through a pilot implementation using Claude Monet's Water Lilies.
